## This defect has a second instance, and it does not have the same fix

Investigating four ALARM-state `rebar/host` alarms on 2026-09-06 (`rebar-container-reaper-not-active`,
`rebar-var-tmp-cleanup-not-active`, `rebar-container-writable-usage-high`, `rebar-var-tmp-usage-high`)
led back to exactly this mechanism, but on the OTHER TWO cap scripts. Filed as
`exorable-gemstone-bluefish` (`1e63-bee1-5ce6-4d8f`) and closed as a duplicate of this ticket; its
evidence is folded in here.

`observability.sh` resolves four cap scripts as siblings of the running probe, not two:

```
 458: DOCKER_CAP_SH=...   /docker-storage-cap.sh
 925: JOURNALD_CAP_SH=... /journald-cap.sh
 999: VARTMP_CAP_SH=...   /vartmp-cap.sh
1092: CONTAINER_CAP_SH=... /container-cap.sh
```

The first two were repaired by the manual copy this ticket records (they are on the host dated
`Sep 5 01:05`, and `docker_storage_used_percent` / `journal_used_percent` publish normally).
**The second two were never placed at all**, so the same failure is still live:

```
bash: /usr/local/bin/vartmp-cap.sh: No such file or directory     rc=127
bash: /usr/local/bin/container-cap.sh: No such file or directory  rc=127
```

Consequences, matching this ticket's two consequence classes exactly:
- gated percent metrics silent: `var_tmp_used_percent` and `container_writable_used_percent` are
  absent from the namespace entirely (0 datapoints in 3h; not in `list-metrics`).
- ungated heartbeats pinned to a false 0: `var_tmp_cleanup_active` and `container_reaper_active`
  publish 0 because `--check-active` returns empty and `case` coerces it — the same
  `journal_cap_in_effect` failure shape described in this ticket's consequence 2, on two more metrics.

## The part that changes AC1

For `docker-storage-cap.sh` / `journald-cap.sh`, "deploy every script the probe resolves" is
sufficient — neither defines an installed path, so their repo basename is the only name they have.

**`vartmp-cap.sh` and `container-cap.sh` are different: they self-install under a different name.**

```
infra/scripts/vartmp-cap.sh:121    VAR_TMP_INSTALLED_PATH="${...:-/usr/local/bin/rebar-vartmp-cap.sh}"
infra/scripts/container-cap.sh:124 CONTAINER_INSTALLED_PATH="${...:-/usr/local/bin/rebar-container-cap.sh}"
```

Their `--install` writes the `rebar-`-prefixed name (it is the `ExecStart` the reaper units point
at). So satisfying AC1 by the installer direction alone would place a SECOND copy at the unprefixed
name, and the box would carry two copies of the same script — the probe reading one, the reaper
timer executing the other, free to drift on the next partial deploy. For these two the
resolver direction is the one that composes; picking the first existing candidate from an ordered
list (installed name, then repo-sibling name) leaves exactly one copy on the host.

## Proven, not inferred: repairing the host does NOT repair the metric

With operator-authorised `vartmp-cap.sh --install` and `container-cap.sh --install` run on
i-00880b2c7f13527c5 at 2026-09-06 01:23Z (both rc=0; `rebar-var-tmp-reaper.timer` and
`rebar-container-reaper.timer` now in force), the truth and what the probe can see disagree:

```
# truth, via the installed prefixed path
vartmp_true=[1]      container_true=[1]
# what the probe actually calls
bash: /usr/local/bin/vartmp-cap.sh: No such file or directory
bash: /usr/local/bin/container-cap.sh: No such file or directory
```

So a host with both reapers correctly installed still publishes `0` for both heartbeats and still
omits both percentages. That isolates this ticket's defect from the host's configuration state:
the two dead-man alarms will keep firing on a now-healthy host until the resolution is fixed, which
is the `journal_cap_in_effect` "false 0 forever" failure reproducing on two more metrics.

## What the alarms were hiding

`/var/tmp` measured 3664 MiB against the 4 GiB budget `--print-env` reports — about **89%**, over
the 85% threshold of `rebar-var-tmp-usage-high`, and all 317,710 files were older than 7 days
(2.85 GB of `rebar-review-rehearsal.*` scratch). `/etc/tmpfiles.d/99-rebar-var-tmp.conf` did not
exist. The alarms were correct and unfalsifiable at the same time.

## Ruled out

Not probe staleness and not truncation: `sha256(/usr/local/bin/rebar-observability.sh)` equals
`sha256(origin/main infra/scripts/observability.sh)` = `6d900dbde913...`, so `aaa31f11f3bc` (the
probe time-budget fix) IS deployed, and `probe_ok` / `probe_truncated` publish normally. No
`terraform apply` is implicated either: all four alarms are already live in AWS from
`monitoring_autodeploy.tf` with the config the code expects (`breaching`, 6/6).

Existing tests cannot catch any of this: `tests/scripts/test_observability_*.py` run
`infra/scripts/observability.sh` in place, where every cap script IS a sibling. The suite exercises
the checkout layout and never the installed layout.
